doc.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Tommy Dorsey records convince him to stay on trombone
summary: Bored with long notes, Barrett is played Tommy Dorsey 78s showing the trombone can carry a melody; Owen also gives him trumpet lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: board, you know, they weighed a ton. Well he brought out one of those, and he had a couple of old 78s, and for our younger viewers, this is kind of funny. I never felt as old as I did when a student came over to my house for a lesson, and this young man was in his early 20s, and I wanted to play — I’m digressing but I’ll get back — but I wanted to play him a record by Tommy Dorsey, and I went to my 78 collection and he said, “what are those? Is that a record?” And I said, “yes, it’s a 78.” And he said, “oh, far out, man, I’ve never seen one of those.” And I thought God, I’m getting old. Anyway, so for our listeners, a 78 is an old, two-sided record, long before LPs they had 78s. They’re real brittle and pretty fragile. Anyway that’s what a 78 is. So anyway, Mr. Owen brought a couple of 78s by Tommy Dorsey and his orchestra, and he said, “Danny, you listen to this man, now he’s going to play the melody on the trombone.” And he put on this 78 and I can’t remember the tune, it could have been Tommy Dorsey’s theme song, “I’m Getting Sentimental Over You,” something like that. And I’d never heard anything like that in my life, and for a while I thought Mr. Owen was putting me on, because I thought it was a French horn. I’d never heard a trombone played like that in my life you know. So he said, “see, if you practiced you could sound like that, and we’ll have solos for you with the band and everything.” So he convinced me into staying on the trombone for the concert band. But later on my folks got me a trumpet from a pawn shop, and Mr. Owen was a fairly accomplished Air Force trumpet player. So he agreed, he was a very kind man, he agreed to meet me after school and he gave me some trumpet lessons. So I wound up playing both of the instruments, although I played trombone in the school band, I played trumpet for fun with other groups.
